name: COMPLETED PROOF

phase_0.boundary_condition: The set of natural numbers ℕ containing the subset A, bounded by the divergence of the reciprocal sum and the existence of arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.

VINIT.justification: The void state before the subset A is defined or the reciprocal sum is evaluated.

TANCH.justification: The terminal anchor representing the complete conjecture statement where divergence implies AP existence.

AFWD.justification: The forward morphism establishing the hypothesis that the sum of reciprocals of A diverges to infinity.

AREV.justification: The reverse morphism representing the failure to derive positive density from divergence, as shown by the primes.

CLINK.justification: The composition linking reciprocal divergence to a density increment for the k=3 case.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-referential identity of the primes, which satisfy divergence but have zero density, anchoring the paradox.

FSPLIT.justification: The split separating the settled k=3 case from the open k≥4 conjecture.

FFUSE.justification: The fusion of the proven k=3 branch and the open k≥4 branch into a single state holding both truth and falsity.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative evaluation where positive density guarantees a 3-term arithmetic progression.

EVALF.justification: The negative evaluation where the general mechanism to convert divergence to density for k≥4 is absent.

ENGAGR.justification: The state holding both the truth of divergence and the truth of zero density simultaneously without resolution.

IFIX.justification: The permanent fixation of the open axiom reciprocal_divergence_to_positive_density in the formal library.

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: No subset A defined; no sum computed; no progression sought.
phase_3.true_description: A set A with divergent reciprocal sum contains an arithmetic progression of length k.
phase_3.false_description: A set A with divergent reciprocal sum does not necessarily contain an arithmetic progression of length k.
phase_3.both_description: The conjecture is true for k=3 (proven) and false for k≥4 (unproven/open), held simultaneously as the current state of knowledge.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the domain with the empty set of natural numbers before defining A.
Apply the forward morphism to establish the hypothesis that the reciprocal sum of A diverges.
Anchor the system with the Prime Number Set as the self-referential counterexample to density.
Branch the domain into the k=3 case and the k≥4 case.
On the T-arm, apply the Bloom-Sisash transference to lift divergence to a density increment.
Compose the density increment with the finite threshold N for Roth's theorem.
Evaluate the T-arm affirmatively: positive density implies a 3-term arithmetic progression exists.
Fix the result of the k=3 proof as a permanent record in the formal library.
On the F-arm, apply the reverse morphism to expose the gap where divergence does not imply density.
Evaluate the F-arm negatively: no general mechanism exists to convert divergence to density for k≥4.
Engage the paradice state where the primes demonstrate both divergence and zero density simultaneously.
Fix the open axiom reciprocal_divergence_to_positive_density as a permanent unresolved constraint.
Fuse the T-arm (proven k=3) and F-arm (open k≥4) into a single dialetheic verdict.
Anchor the entire system at the closure of Erdős Problem #3, holding the B state.
